entries.appliesTo: no bound party — amends the code-wide statutory definition of 'person'

sources.family: SECTION 1 (amending Tenn. Code Ann. § 1-3-105(a)(20)) — '(20) "Person": (A) Includes a corporation, firm, company, or association; and (B) Does not include artificial intelligence, a computer algorithm, a software program, computer hardware, or any type of machine'

flags: definitions-only act: amends the general definition of 'person' in Title 1 (rules of code construction) to exclude AI/algorithms/software/hardware/machines; imposes no compliance duty on any party

category is a forced choice — none of company/criminal/public-sector/education fits a code-construction amendment with no bound party; coded public-sector because the definition governs interpretation of state statutes
no penalty or enforcement provision in the text — exposure omitted (silence is silence)
not a duplicate: SB 837 was 'Substituted for: House Bill No. 849' — SB 837 is the surviving vehicle (legiscan.js shows only a 'crossfiled' relation to HB 849, no replaced-by)
